newsitem.title: USA: Jones lawyers file questions for Clinton - CBS.
newsitem.headline: Jones lawyers file questions for Clinton - CBS.

text.p: Lawyers pursuing Paula Jones' sexual harassment suit have prepared six questions for President Clinton to answer under oath, including whether he ever "requested sex from her," the CBS Evening News reported on Saturday.
The six questions, known as "interrogatories," mark the first step in the pre-trial process and indicate that Jones is hoping to move quickly to trial, CBS said.
The lawyers plan to ask Clinton:
-- if he was alone with Jones in a room at the Excelsior Hotel on May 8, 1991;
-- if he ever requested sex from Jones;
-- who, if anyone, he asked to bring Jones to the room;
-- if he ever discussed Jones with her boss, the head of an Arkansas state agency;
-- whether he discussed her later charges against him with any Arkansas state troopers;
-- whether he got jobs or money for those troopers.
Jones has accused the president of asking her for "a type of sex" when she was an Arkansas state employee and the two were alone in an Arkansas hotel room in 1991. Clinton denies the charge.
The Supreme Court ruled on May 27 that Jones could go ahead with her sexual harassment lawsuit, which Clinton had sought to block at least until he was out of office.
